latest_release.body:
## What's Changed
* increase chunk size from 512 bytes to 64 KB for HTTP response reading by @YasirAlibrahem in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/1511
* fix(wikipedia): accept mobile (m.wikipedia.org) URLs by @GopalGB in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/1850
* fix: handle None sys.stdout.encoding in CLI output by @octo-patch in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/1656
* Add language parameter for the audio transcription by @hchmch in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/1295
* Perf: Optimize non-seekable stream buffering using shutil.copyfileobj by @YasirAlibrahem in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/1510
* Use frozenset for OMML direct tag lookup by @Amitanand983 in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/1919
* fix(wikipedia): drop the site suffix from italicised titles by @macjayz in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/2458
* Consolidate tests by format and strengthen regression coverage by @afourney in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/2579
* Replace local parser mocks with real conversion fixtures by @afourney in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/2586
* Test real installed OCR plugin discovery by @afourney in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/2588
* Test real CLI file-type parsing and CU result formatting by @afourney in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/2592
* Test PowerPoint missing text with real fixtures and shared vectors by @afourney in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/2594
* Test MCP input errors with real conversions by @afourney in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/2597
* Restore JSON regression coverage for late non-ASCII text by @afourney in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/2601
* Bump the magika dependency by @afourney in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/2722
* Bump Mammoth dependency to >=1.12.2,<2 by @afourney in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/2729
* Require certifi>=2026.10.19 for updated CA trust by @afourney in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/2730
* Update Black, Pillow, and Windows ARM Cryptography baselines by @afourney in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/2731

## New Contributors
* @YasirAlibrahem made their first contribution in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/1511
* @GopalGB made their first contribution in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/1850
* @octo-patch made their first contribution in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/1656
* @hchmch made their first contribution in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/1295
* @Amitanand983 made their first contribution in https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/pull/1919

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown/compare/v0.1.8...v0.1.9

detail.readme_excerpt:
# MarkItDown

[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/markitdown.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/markitdown/)
![PyPI - Downloads](https://img.shields.io/pypi/dd/markitdown)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> MarkItDown performs I/O with the privileges of the current process. Like open() or requests.get(), it will access resources that the process itself can access. Sanitize your inputs in untrusted environments, and call the narrowest `convert_*` function needed for your use case (e.g., `convert_stream()`, or `convert_local()`). See the [Security Considerations](#security-considerations) section of the documentation for more information.

MarkItDown is a lightweight Python utility for converting various files to Markdown for use with LLMs and related text analysis pipelines. To this end, it is most comparable to [textract](https://github.com/deanmalmgren/textract), but with a focus on preserving important document structure and content as Markdown (including: headings, lists, tables, links, etc.) While the output is often reasonably presentable and human-friendly, it is meant to be consumed by text analysis tools -- and may not be the best option for high-fidelity document conversions for human consumption.

MarkItDown currently supports the conversion from:

- PDF
- PowerPoint
- Word
- Excel
- Images (EXIF metadata and captioning)
- Audio (EXIF metadata and speech transcription)
- HTML
- Text-based formats (CSV, JSON, XML)
- ZIP files (iterates over contents)
- YouTube URLs
- EPubs
- ... and more!

NOTE: Image captioning and speech transcription rely on web-hosted services.

## Why Markdown?

Markdown is extremely close to plain text, with minimal markup or formatting, but still
provides a way to represent important document structure. Mainstream LLMs, such as
OpenAI's GPT-4o, natively "_speak_" Markdown, and often incorporate Markdown into their
responses unprompted. This suggests that they have been trained on vast amounts of
Markdown-formatted text, and understand it well. As a side benefit, Markdown conventions
are also highly token-efficient.

## Prerequisites
MarkItDown requires Python 3.10 through 3.14. It is recommended to use a virtual environment to avoid dependency conflicts.

With the standard Python installation, you can create and activate a virtual environment using the following commands:

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
```

If using `uv`, you can create a virtual environment with:

```bash
uv venv --python=3.12 .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
# NOTE: Be sure to use 'uv pip install' rather than just 'pip install' to install packages in this virtual environment
```

If you are using Anaconda, you can create a virtual environment with:

```bash
conda create -n markitdown python=3.12
conda activate markitdown
```

## Installation

To install MarkItDown, use pip: `pip install 'markitdown[all]'`. Alternatively, you can install it from the source:

```bash
git clone git@github.com:microsoft/markitdown.git
cd markitdown
pip install
